messages:
maria: FYI, onboarding run for `mistral-8b-qat` flagged a bunch of chat regression tests — looks like some special tokens got shifted after our HF->Redwood conversion. anyone seen this pattern before?

dan: ugh. seen shifts when added_tokens.json ordering differs. can you paste the tokenizer snippet? :eyes: 

maria: here's the added_tokens block from the HF repo we converted (copied):

```json
"added_tokens": [
  {"content": "<|bos|>", "id": 50000},
  {"content": "<|eos|>", "id": 50001},
  {"content": "<|pad|>", "id": 50002},
  {"content": "<|unk|>", "id": 50003}
]
```

maria: and the tokenizer we ended up shipping in Redwood after conversion: 

```json
"added_tokens": [
  {"content": "<|bos|>", "id": 50003},
  {"content": "<|eos|>", "id": 50004},
  {"content": "<|pad|>", "id": 50005},
  {"content": "<|unk|>", "id": 50006}
]
```

maria: basically +3 offset on all special ids. chat templates use absolute ids in a couple places, so that blew up.

sasha: hmm, why did conversion add +3? convert script normally preserves explicit ids. did HF tokenizer have a `merge` step or we re-serialized with different base vocab length?

convert-bot: hf->redwood conversion job finished: tokenizer.json rewritten, added_tokens preserved but IDs normalized based on target vocab size. patch: normalizing ids by appending to vocab tail.

dan: there we go — bot normalized instead of preserving explicit id fields. not ideal for special tokens.

ben: quick triage — are downstream chat templates referencing tokens by id or by token string? if by string we could be OK.

maria: some codepaths (legacy chatfmt serializer) store BOS/EOS as numeric ids in the model metadata for faster decoding. so numeric drift causes immediate mismatch.

tokenizer-bot: suggestion: run `python -c 'from transformers import PreTrainedTokenizerFast; t = PreTrainedTokenizerFast.from_pretrained("./tokenizer"); print(t.convert_tokens_to_ids(["<|bos|>", "<|eos|>"]))'` to verify.

maria: ran that locally — HF tokenizer shows [50000,50001] while Redwood's runtime tokenizer shows [50003,50004].

sasha: possible fixes: 1) update conversion script to honor explicit `id` fields in added_tokens and remap vocab insertion points; 2) add a migration step that rewrites model metadata to use token strings instead of hard ids; 3) fallback mapping table at runtime to translate old ids.

ben: prefer (1) for long-term. we should also run a smoke that checks all models for special token id stability during import. can someone open an infra ticket?

dan: opening ticket now: ENG-ML-4267. assigned to me + sasha. will add a blocker flag for production imports.

maria: for immediate mitigation, can we ship a small patch that rewrites the model metadata on import when id mismatch is detected? simple map: for each added_token, lookup by content and replace id field in metadata.

sasha: yes that sounds low-risk. I'll add a tiny step in the converter: if any added_token has explicit `id`, set `keep_ids=True` and extend base vocab instead of normalizing. falling back to rewrite metadata if conflicting indices found.

convert-bot: patch queued: `preserve_added_token_ids` flag toggled for onboarding batch. running validations.

maria: after running the conversion with the flag, chat regressions went away on the small sample set. pushing full eval now. :thumbsup:

ben: long term action items: - add unit test that asserts BOS/EOS/PAD/UNK id parity across HF and Redwood artifacts - add CI gate on model onboarding - document conversion flag in onboarding playbook

dan: noted. I'll attach logs to ENG-ML-4267.

maria: thanks all — close loop after full eval completes.

sasha: also opened a tiny PR to change legacy chatfmt serializer to prefer token strings if present — backward compatible.

maria: nice. re-run looks green. planning to promote to staging tomorrow.

ben: :party_parrot: good catch, folks.
